column11: Verquvo, CMS Medicare Part D 2024 (drug_demand, brand Verquvo): $49,680,166.72 over 11,127 beneficiaries = $4,464.83 a beneficiary a year. This is the basis the book prices on and the same method amgn_abp_206.csv uses. The series is consistent and rising as the launch matures: $2,240 a beneficiary in 2021, $3,351 in 2022, $4,189 in 2023. For scale rather than for the arithmetic, the unit price under it is $49,680,166.72 over 2,271,002 dosage units = $21.876 a tablet, so a full labelled year of 365 tablets is $7,985 gross; the current pharmacy acquisition cost is close to it, CMS NADAC putting Verquvo 10 mg at $22.72787 a tablet effective 2026-10-21, a labelled year of $8,296
column12: a price per patient treated in a year, not per full year on drug, which is what makes it consistent with discontinuation_pct below: $4,465 / $7,985 = 0.5592, exactly the share of a labelled year the stopping rate is derived from. Pairing the $7,985 labelled year with the same 0.4408 would count the shortfall twice. The Part D population skews to 65 and over, which for a post-hospitalisation heart failure product is close to the real population rather than a distortion

Direction: chronic heart failure is a crowded retail pharmacy class where Entresto and the SGLT2 inhibitors compete for formulary position, so a deep rebate is the right expectation rather than a shallow oncology one. column11: measured on Verquvo's own patients: drug_demand Verquvo, CMS Medicare Part D 2024, 2,271,002 dosage units over 11,127 beneficiaries = 204.10 tablets a beneficiary. the current VERQUVO label, DailyMed SPL setid 17056d73-1b1b-4bf2-9c07-b7a9367f0d6d, version 13, effective 2026-02-06 gives one tablet once daily after a four-week titration from 2.5 mg through 5 mg to the 10 mg target, so a labelled year is 365 tablets whatever the strength reached. 204.10 / 365 = 0.5592 of a labelled year, and 1 - 0.5592 = 0.4408 of the stock stops each year
column12: the share of a labelled year filled has risen every year of the launch, 0.3091 in 2021, 0.4344 in 2022, 0.5120 in 2023, 0.5592 in 2024, which is what a growing product looks like rather than improving persistence: a cohort full of mid-year starters fills less of a year than a settled one. So the stopping rate here is the high end of the plausible range and will fall further as the base matures. It is carried at the 2024 figure because that is the year the price above is measured on and the two have to describe the same patients. Against it in the other direction: VICTORIA (NCT02861534) ran a median 10.8 months with 10.4% permanent discontinuation for adverse events, so all-cause stopping in a real population being well above that is the expected direction

column12: the prevalent pool is set equal to the annual incidence and that understates it, which is the thing to argue with in this file. Children with dilated cardiomyopathy live for years on medical therapy, so the number alive with the disease at any moment is a multiple of a year's diagnoses rather than equal to it. No US prevalence of paediatric dilated cardiomyopathy was found that a reader could open, so the figure is left at the one that is sourced rather than grossed up by a survival multiple nobody published. The layer is therefore low and knowably so. Replace it when a US prevalence is published

column11: two published shares multiplied. Dilated cardiomyopathy is 51% of paediatric cardiomyopathy cases, against 42% hypertrophic and 3% restrictive (the same registry series, N Engl J Med 2003;348:1647-1655); VALOR excludes hypertrophic and restrictive cardiomyopathy, single-ventricle physiology, a morphologic systemic right ventricle and unoperated or residual significant congenital malformations, so the dilated share is what the trial's physiology requirement amounts to. And 73% of children with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy had symptomatic heart failure at diagnosis (Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Registry; Wilkinson et al., 'Treating children with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy', Am J Cardiol 2009;104:281-286, doi:10.1016/j.amjcard.2009.03.033, 569 children), which is the trial's symptomatic chronic heart failure requirement. 0.51 x 0.73 = 0.3723, about 308 children a year
column12: the remaining entry criteria are not narrowed for and this leans high as a result: VALOR also requires an ejection fraction under 45% within three months of randomisation, stable background heart failure therapy, clinical stability and at least 3 kg of body weight. No published share covers those, so they are left in the penetration judgement rather than estimated here

column11: a share of the pool above, set against what the molecule has to displace
column12: a judgement, and the one to argue with after the pool. The case for it being high: no oral heart failure drug is approved for children at all, paediatric cardiologists prescribe enalapril, carvedilol and spironolactone off label on adult evidence, and a labelled paediatric claim with a dosing table would be the only one in the class. The case for it being low: vericiguat is an add-on to that same background therapy rather than a replacement for it, the paediatric prescriber base is a few hundred centres, and Entresto already carries a paediatric claim from the PANORAMA-HF programme, so the first-mover argument is weaker than it looks. A fifth of the eligible pool is the middle of those two

column11: the published transition chain for Cardiovascular, read from the Phase 2 entry because VALOR is registered as Phase 2/3 and has not separated the stages: 0.210 Phase 2 to Phase 3 (n=252), 0.552 Phase 3 to NDA (n=105), 0.825 NDA to approval (n=80). BIO / Informa Pharma Intelligence (Biomedtracker) / QLS Advisors, 'Clinical Development Success Rates and Contributing Factors 2011-2020', Figure 2 page 7
column12: low, and deliberately not adjusted upward. The case for a higher number is real: this is a paediatric extension of a molecule with a positive adult Phase 3 behind it, the mechanism is established and the primary endpoint is a biomarker, change in NT-proBNP at week 16, rather than an outcome. The published chain does not know any of that, and the rates are commercial rather than technical, so a programme stopped on portfolio grounds counts as a failure here. Replace it with the Phase 3 chain, 0.552 x 0.825 = 0.4554, when Merck states VALOR has passed its Phase 2 stage, with 0.825 on a positive readout, or with 0 on a failed one. Primary completion is 2032-04-15, so this sits a long way out
